title: Quantization profile benchmarking harness for FP16/INT8/INT4 — perf/quality sweep and regression alerts
creator: Priya Menon
description: Goal: Build a reproducible benchmarking and load-testing harness that runs performance vs quality sweeps across quantization profiles (FP16, INT8, INT4) and automatically detects regressions in p95 latency and generation quality. Background: We need empirical guidance for production quantization profiles for common model families (decoder-only LLaMA-style and encoder-decoder for embeddings/seq2seq) so Platform and Model Ops can pick defaults that balance cost and accuracy. Current gaps: ad-hoc perf runs, manual quality checks, no automated regression alerts when a quantized build drops below quality thresholds. Scope: - Implement an automated runner that can schedule and execute sweeps across quantized binaries/container images and model variants. - Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, request/sec, GPU utilization, and memory footprint. - Run quality checks using a mixed evaluation set: a curated prompt set (200 prompts) covering open-ended generation, instruction following, and classification/regression tasks, plus a held-out eval set for embeddings similarity. - Compute quality metrics: LM perplexity (where applicable), token-level and sequence-level BLEU/ROUGE for synthetic tasks, and cosine similarity on embeddings with a thresholded regression detector. - Integrate with Prometheus/Grafana for time-series, and with the regression-alerting pipeline to open issues when a quantized profile crosses defined failure criteria. - Provide automation for canary jobs, and a report generator producing CSV/Markdown artifacts and a summary dashboard. Constraints: Tests must be repeatable and parameterized (batch size, seq length distribution, concurrency). Harness should run both in local k8s dev cluster (min scale) and on dedicated infra used in perf lab. Compliance: ensure no customer PII is used in eval prompts. Deliverables: runner code, CI workflows, Grafana dashboards, a Confluence runbook, and a triage playbook for quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end harness that runs a quantization sweep (FP16, INT8, INT4) over at least two model sizes and produces a single CSV with perf and quality columns
2) Perf metrics captured: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, memory; quality metrics captured: embedding cosine, BLEU/ROUGE, perplexity (where applicable)
3) Automatic regression detection: alerts if p95 increases >20% or embedding cosine drops >0.05 (configurable thresholds) compared to baseline FP16 run
4) Grafana dashboard showing comparative curves across quantization profiles and a linkable report artifact produced at end of run
5) CI job that runs a lightweight smoke sweep on PRs and a scheduled full sweep nightly in perf project namespace

comments: 2025-02-18 Priya Menon: Initial ticket created. Drafted scope and primary metrics. Early ask from Platform about recommending INT8 defaults for 13B family if perf gains >2x with <0.03 embedding delta.

2025-02-20 Ethan Cole: Spike completed for runner prototype. Built a k8s Job-based runner that can launch three image variants in parallel. Prototype measures tokens/sec and p95 with a synthetic seq length distribution. Pushed prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3472

2025-02-24 Research (Marisol Vega): Curated eval set (200 prompts) uploaded to GCS under gs://redwood-perf/evalsets/quant-sweep/2025-02-24. Includes held-out embeddings pairs for cosine testing. Dataset sanitized for PII.
2025-02-27 SRE (Liam Zhang): Added GPU exporter and node-exporter labels to perf-lab cluster. Confirmed Prometheus scrape for custom tokens/sec metric. Updated infra playbook in Confluence.

2025-03-02 Ethan Cole: Implemented regression detector. Heuristic: compare current profile to FP16 baseline from last full run; if p95 > baseline * 1.2 OR embedding cosine < baseline - 0.05 for >50 prompts, mark as regression. Created initial PR for detector: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3501

2025-03-04 Priya Menon: Review feedback from PM and Research: lower the embedding threshold to 0.04 for decoder-only models and add sequence-level coverage checks. Also asked to capture tokenization differences as a separate column. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly.
notes: Decision log: Use FP16 run as canonical baseline for regression comparisons because it's the closest to exporter full-precision behavior in our runtime.

Tradeoff: INT4 offers largest perf gains on small models but shows larger variance on open-ended generation. For production defaults we will require a passing quality gate on both embedding and generation metrics.
Run cadence: nightly full sweep (long) and PR-triggered mini-sweep (short) that runs a sampled 20-prompt subset and measures tokens/sec and p95 only.
Follow-ups: Add support for mixed-precision kernels in runner and tie to kernel selection matrix for release notes in runtime-1.22.
